name: Indian Valley

dates.altered: The surveyor found the fabric 'Bad' and records the avenue of locust trees, the curved yard fence and the piazza round the 'Island Room' as all destroyed by the time of the survey.
dates.note: The survey's own form prints 'Date built: (approx) In the 184-0 s.' -- 1840s with an OCR hyphen. The Library's catalogue line prints 'after 1840 Initial Construction'. No other date was found.

quotes.text: The natural beauty which in former years surrounded this old place has been removed. The avenue of locust trees, one-half mile to the main road, the curved fence about the yard, the piasza surrounding the "island Room" on the side facing the river, features which added to the beauty of the place have all been destroyed.

note: Written 5 Sep 2026 for Tranche 2. The plainest record in this cluster, and it is here for that reason: a two-storey brick house in the Ohio Valley of the 1840s with one-storey wings, brick and frame partitions and wood shingles, surveyed while it was failing, with no ornament described and no dimension given. It is what the node calls the stratum -- the house the region was already building -- and the surveyor never once uses the word Greek. Note that the piazza the surveyor mourns is on the RIVER side and is named for the room behind it, which is a Louisiana-and-Ohio habit rather than an Appalachian one; the node's geography lists the Ohio Valley and this is what that inclusion buys.
